messages.subject: Re: JGR and site-library
messages.body_plain:
From the docs:

As from R 2.5.0 R will automatically make use of a site-specific library
‘R_HOME/site-library’ if this exists (it does not in a vanilla R 
installation).

Could JGR honor this perhaps?
If I understand correctly, that is what you read from the registry,

[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\R-core\R]
"InstallPath"="C:\\Program Files\\R\\R-2.6.2"
"Current Version"="2.6.2"

So you just would need to search for site library as a subdirectory of 
this location.





Simon Urbanek wrote:
> 
> On Feb 26, 2008, at 4:34 AM, Erich Neuwirth wrote:
> 
>> I am using JGR 1.5-8 on Windows XP with R 2.6.2.
>> I keep all the additional packages in site-library instead of library.
>> R honors this and finds the packages without any problems.
>> When I start JGR, however, it tells me that it needs to download
>> packages, does it, and then exits with an error message.
>> Next time started it does the same thing.
>> Moving JGR, rJava, JavaGD and iplots from site-library to library
>> immediately solves the problem.
>>
>> Should this be fixed in JGR?
>> Can it be solved temporarily by setting an environment variable?
>>
> 
> On unix you can set R_LIBS accordingly. When run the first time, JGR 
> saves this setting to its preference file, so you only need to specify 
> it once.
> On Windows, you have no choice, because the check is performed based on 
> the registry setting of R before the preference file is read. How do you 
> set a non-standard location? Clearly .Rprofile is not an option, because 
> that requires a running R already.
> I could add an option such that you could add let's say a registry key 
> to override the path that JGR is using, but I'm not sure how compatible 
> that would be ...
> 
> Cheers,
> Simon
> 
> 
>

messages.body_plain:
Hi Markus,

I had a look at JGR-1.5.9, and now I made thorougher tests with
JGR-1-5-11. (I see now that JGR-1.5-12 is out today, I will check it
soon too, at last, when it reaches CRAN...)

The overprint bug seems to have disappeared -- thanks. The other three
bugs (AltGr+key popups, fontsize, and lack of some handy old
keybindings) still persist, and there is one additional bug as well...

I now prepared a reproducible (I hope) example for the fontsize bug:
1. start JGR
2. open a new, clean editor window (with the leftmost button in the toolbox)
3. paste the followings (or sg similar):
aaaaaaaaaaaaa(bbbbbbbbb)
#aaaaaaaaaaaaa(bbbbbbbbb)
aaaaaaaaaaaaa(bbbbbbbbb)

4. decrease fontsize 4 times (Editor window/Tools/Decrease Font Size)
-->(Clipboard02.png)
5. go to the end of first line -->(Clipboard04.png)
6. go down one line by pressing the down arrow  -->(Clipboard05.png)
7. go right two characters: now we are at the "end of line" -->(Clipboard06.png)
8. go down one line -->(Clipboard07.png)

As it seems character sizes for comments seem to be managed somehow
separately. If I remove the # from line 2, character sizes are
calculated correctly again. Increasing font size twice exerts a
similar effect.

A further new bug is that cursor positions are calculated incorrectly
in this release. See in Clipboard09.png: if I click somewhere in the
editor window, the cursor will be placed some characters to the right
from the position of the mouse pointer. Similarly navigating up and
down in the text often displaces the cursor some characters to the
right.
(I hope that this has aready been corrected with JGR 1-5-12...)

Best regards, and thanks for maintaining and developing JGR:
Bálint

run the "run rtest" and "run rtest2" perfectly, i.e. the JVM calling

messages.subject: RJDBC fetch question
messages.body_plain:
I'm working with RJDBC fetch'es from a postgresql database.  For
database text fields, <null> is assigned <NA> in R but numeric fields
<null> end up as 0.  Is this the desired behavior? Should I have the
database setup differently?  I hacked a fix in the fetch method at
line ~223 of class.R (see below). Is this appropriate?

Thanks!
Tom

a <- .jcall(res@jr, "S", "getString", i)
l[[i]][j] <- if (is.null(a)) NA else .jcall(res@jr, "D", "getDouble", i)
